preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.
The number of edges m is between n-1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(d in [-1, 0, 1] for d in d_list)
preconditions.description: Each vertex requirement di is -1, 0, or 1.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices within the valid range.
The number of degree requirements matches the number of vertices.
The number of edges matches m.

postconditions.expression: is_impossible or (k >= 0 and len(edge_indices) == k and all(1 <= idx <= m for idx in edge_indices))
postconditions.description: Either the output is -1 indicating impossibility, or it contains a non-negative count k and exactly k valid edge indices between 1 and m.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and all((d_list[i-1] == -1) or (degree_in_subset[i] % 2 == d_list[i-1]) for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, for every vertex i, if di is not -1, the degree of vertex i in the selected subset modulo 2 equals di.

postconditions.expression: is_impossible and (sum(d for d in d_list if d != -1) % 2 != 0)
postconditions.description: If the sum of required parities (excluding -1) is odd, no solution exists, and the output must be -1.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and all(idx in edge_indices for idx in edge_indices)
postconditions.description: The output edge indices correspond to a valid subset of the input edges.
